newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls as liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls as liquidity improves.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate ended lower as more liquidity entered the market, dealers said.
The rate ended 6.50 percent against 8.8/9.0 previously, after trading between 6.50 and 8.80.
"I think people are long on dollar/ringgit. They have been buying dollar and throwing ringgit and some are landing on the overnight," said a money market dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said large local banks which have been providing liquidity to the market in recent sessions were reticent.
The additional liquidity was believed to be provided by foreign banks, said a dealer at another local bank.
The fall of the overnight rate followed that of all the other rates.
Earlier, other interbank rates were flat to lower due to the improving liquidity.
The one-, two- and three-week money were at 7.50/80 percent against 8.0/9.0 on Tuesday, dealers said.
The one-month rate was at 8.0 percent against 7.5/8.0.
Three month money was at 7.50/80 percent from 7.50/8.0.
In the futures market, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contracts which were all lower in the morning ended flat to weaker.
The June 1997 contract was down three basis points to 92.47, or an implied yield of 7.53 percent.
September 1997 contract was unchanged at 92.59, or 7.41 percent and December also steady at 92.62, or 7.38 percent.
